report.narrative_markdown:
## Company overview

Freedom Holding Corp. (FRHC) is a financial conglomerate in the Financial Services sector, with a market capitalization of $10.82B. Through its subsidiaries it provides securities brokerage, dealing, market making, investment research and counseling, retail and commercial banking, and insurance products. It reports four segments: Brokerage, Banking, Insurance and Other. The Brokerage segment covers investment banking, margin lending against customer collateral, capital raising and debt capital markets solutions. The shares trade at $169.65, within a 52-week range of $107.97 to $178.00.

## Financial commentary

Revenue has grown steadily, from $795.69M in fiscal 2023 to $1.64B in 2024, $1.99B in 2025 and $2.17B in 2026. The latest reported revenue growth rate is 27.8%. Profit has been far less steady. Net income was $205.14M in 2023, rose to $379.11M in 2024, dropped to $76.29M in 2025 and recovered to $153.33M in 2026. The net margin is 8.4% and return on equity is 10.7%. Debt/Equity is 1.82, and the company pays no dividend. Revenue expansion has therefore not translated consistently into earnings.

## Comps commentary

The comparison uses P/B as the primary multiple, against peers including Interactive Brokers, Charles Schwab, Robinhood, Virtu Financial and Hilltop Holdings. FRHC's P/B of 6.8 is 78% above the peer median of 3.8. Its trailing P/E of 67.3 is 282% above the peer median of 17.6, and its forward P/E of 37.7 is 156% above the median of 14.7. Revenue growth of 27.8% is 6% above the peer median of 26.3%, so the growth edge is small relative to the valuation gap. ROE of 10.7% is 55% below the peer median of 23.6%, and the dividend yield of 0.0% is 100% below the median of 1.3%. The market is paying a notable premium for a company with weaker profitability than its peers and no income return.

## Risk commentary

The filing risk data was unavailable for this report, so no company-specific risks can be ranked here. The financial figures point to areas worth watching: volatile net income, moderate profitability relative to peers, and leverage reflected in a Debt/Equity of 1.82. The premium valuation also leaves the shares exposed if growth slows. Recent news covers a chess championship sponsorship, an institutional share purchase and a "greenest companies" recognition. One headline suggests the stock could be 64% overvalued, but none of this news relates directly to filing risks.
